name: Netherlands

authorities.note: The competent authority and CSIRT depend on your sector. Confirm which one applies to you before relying on this.

incidentDeadlines.of: becoming aware of a significant incident
incidentDeadlines.content: Early warning: whether the incident is suspected to be unlawful/malicious and whether it could have cross-border impact.

incidentDeadlines.of: becoming aware of a significant incident
incidentDeadlines.content: Incident notification: initial assessment, severity and impact, and any indicators of compromise.
Final report: detailed description, root cause, applied and ongoing mitigations, and any cross-border impact.

cra.law: Cyber Resilience Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/2847, Article 14 (reporting applies from 11 September 2026)
cra.note: NCSC-NL is the Dutch CSIRT designated as coordinator on ENISA's list (checked 2026-10-19). It applies if your main establishment is in the Netherlands, i.e. where cybersecurity decisions about your products are predominantly taken (Art. 14(7)).

penalties: Up to €10M or 2% of global annual turnover. Management can be held personally accountable.
pointers: Determine whether you are an essential or important entity, and your sector's competent authority.
Register with your competent authority if in scope.
Keep evidence of your risk-management measures ready to produce if audited.
disclaimer: Penthera provides readiness, evidence, and self-assessment tooling only. It is not legal advice and does not certify or guarantee compliance. Confirm your obligations with your competent authority (RDI) or a qualified advisor.
